rows.title: Real-world creatine supplementation: a large-scale cross-sectional study of use, knowledge, and experiences.
rows.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
rows.focus: Cross-sectional survey of 2,178 recent creatine users found high continuation intent and satisfaction but substantial gaps between expected and perceived benefits. Self-reported side effects were more common among women, and knowledge about creatine was positively associated with perceived benefit and satisfaction. Observational self-report evidence cannot establish efficacy, optimal dose, or causality.
